| _doc | How the abyss warns you as you fall (scripts/match/abyss_fx.gd danger_depth: the red tint and vignette; scripts/match/abyss_fall_sfx.gd warn_db / warn_rate: the heartbeat warning). Depths are metres under the lowest island lip around you. Nothing shows until start_depth, so a small dip under an island's height is free; from there the danger rises smoothly (curve = share of the way to the point of no return, to the power curve) to 1 at the kill depth (Hunter.abyss_kill_y). Rising faster than the glider lift (AbyssFx.RISE_OFF) or climbing back above start_depth lets go. warn_*: the warning heartbeat starts at danger warn_from, at warn_db_min dB and warn_rate_min beats a second, and rises to warn_db_max dB and warn_rate_max at full danger. edge_from: danger where the crimson screen-edge rings start (they ramp up to full at 1). |

Trait drift (GARDEN.md section 3, lever 3; scripts/home/base_drift.gd): with farm_build.json base_mode on, once per in-game day at home each Boki's four traits (0..1) move a small step toward the average of its friends (base life bonds at or above base_life friend_at). Rivals do not pull.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| step | 0.03 |
| step_doc | share of the gap between a Boki's trait and its friends' average that closes each in-game day. |
| week_days | 7 |
| week_days_doc | in-game days in a drift week; the cap below resets when a Boki's week ends. |
| week_cap | 0.12 |
| week_cap_doc | most a single trait may move (either way, summed) in one drift week, in trait units (0..1). |
| young_stages | ["Hatchling", "Youngling"] |
| young_stages_doc | Care.STAGES names (by level) that drift at the full step and week_cap; GARDEN.md 3 lever 3: a base of brave Boki makes a timid baby braver. |
| adult_share | 0.15 |
| adult_share_doc | share (0..1) of step and week_cap a Grown or Elder Boki gets, so adults barely move (0.15: at most 0.018 per trait per drift week). |
| bands | [0.33, 0.67] |
| bands_doc | trait values at which a trait changes band (low, middle, high); crossing one writes a journal line. |
| words | {"bravery": ["braver", "shyer"], "loyalty": ["more loyal", "more independent"], "temper": ["hotter-tempered", "calmer"], "curiosity": ["more curious", "more settled"]} |
| words_doc | per trait: [line when it rises, line when it falls], written as 'is getting <word>' in the Boki's journal. |

## base_echo (`content/rules/base_echo.json`)

Echo Steps, a call-and-answer dance on four humming stones (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 4.2, game 2; scripts/home/echo_steps.gd). Only with farm_build.json base_mode on. The lead hops a pattern across the stones on the beat and you answer it with W, A, S, D; in the last round you lead and the rival copies. Hits and streaks score. Solo (the stones lead) with one rested Boki out, against the next rested Boki with two. Units: beats at bpm, milliseconds for the hit window, seconds otherwise; joy and trust are 0-100 points.

## base_kite (`content/rules/base_kite.json`)

Kite Tow (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md 4.2 game 7, scripts/home/base_kite.gd). Only with farm_build.json base_mode on, and only on Kitewind Ridge. Your Boki glides on a kite round one loop through twelve rings, steered with A and D; Speed sets the pace and a missed ring costs a second. Space flaps the kite up over the high rings; flaps are limited and updraft vents give one back. A lap is raced against a visiting kite whose stats are yours times the cup round's min_ratio (garden_prizes.json kite), so prizes, the first win of the day and the cup come with it. Units: metres, seconds, metres a second; joy is 0-100 points.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|

| loop_r | 6.5 |
| glide_h | 3 |
| loop_doc | The loop is a circle of loop_r round the kite stand, flown counter-clockwise glide_h above the stand; the rings sit evenly round it, the first half a gap after the start, and the lap ends back at the start. |

Each runs one leg and hands the baton on at a mark; your two hand-offs are the Dash's cheer press on the timing bar. Prizes and the cup: garden_prizes.json 'relay'. Units: seconds; joy is 0-100 points, bonds -1..1.

## blight_nests (`content/rules/blight_nests.json`)

Blight nests (scripts/match/blight_nests.gd, docs/SPAWNS.md): the only place Skitters come from. Fixed spots picked from the match seed, the same on every client; each holds a fixed stock, stirs warn_s before Skitters climb out, and once empty stays empty for cooldown_s. Breaking a nest pays like a small camp.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| per_island | [1, 1, 2] |
| _per_island | nests on an island, by its danger (outer, middle, core) |
| stock | [6, 7, 8] |
| _stock | Skitters a full nest holds, by island danger |
| cooldown_s | 300 |
| _cooldown_s | seconds an empty or broken nest stays empty before it fills (and regrows) again |
| warn_s | 2 |
| _warn_s | seconds a nest pulses and hisses before Skitters climb out |
| wake_r | 9 |
| _wake_r | a hunter this close (on its level, in sight) stirs the nest |
| noise_k | 0.6 |
| _noise_k | a loud noise (shot, blast, chest; Blight noise table) stirs a nest within this share of its reach |
| shriek_r | 22 |
| _shriek_r | a Warden's shriek stirs nests this close: they release what they hold, never more |
| area_r | 26 |
| area_cap | 8 |
| _area_cap | at most this many Skitters alive within area_r of a nest; the rest wait in it |
| pop_xp | 80 |
| _pop_xp | XP for each hunter of the breaking squad within 14 m (a knock pays 90) |
| tide_s | 40 |
| _tide_s | the tide: every tide_s (on the match clock) the nearest stocked nest within tide_r of each squad outside the ring stirs |
| tide_r | 45 |
| space_m | 16 |
| _space_m | nests keep this far apart, 9 m from camps, exits, Warden posts and drop spots, and out of lairs |

## boki_fly (`content/rules/boki_fly.json`)

Fliers in the garden (scripts/home/boki_fly.gd, BokiRig's hover, glide and flare clips). A species whose look has wings (its species JSON colors.wing) takes to the air while it roams (BaseLife's Roam) a zone listed in zones, and while it crosses a gap (a bridge over the void, the leap to another isle, The Dash's jump). Each flight picks a height in height (m over the ground); it rises at climb and comes down at sink (m/s), hovering while it stands and gliding while it moves. It flares for flare_s (s) as it touches down: the flare starts sink x flare_s / 2 m up, so the feet land halfway through it. Then it walks.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| zones | ["ridge"] |
| zones_doc | Garden zones where a roaming flier stays in the air: Kitewind Ridge. |
| height | [0.5, 1.5] |
| climb | 1.6 |
| sink | 1.4 |
| flare_s | 0.4 |
| gap_lead | 0.5 |
| vent_r | 1 |
| vent_r_doc | m from an updraft vent (ZoneVents) within which a flier is over it. |
| vent_h | 3 |
| vent_h_doc | m over the ground a flier rises to over a vent; off it, it glides back down at sink to a fresh height. |
| vent_climb | 4 |
| vent_climb_doc | m/s a flier rises over a vent (the usual climb is slower). |
| vent_pull | 0.3 |
| vent_pull_doc | Chance (0..1) that a roaming flier's next goal is a vent instead of any open ground. |
| gap_lead_doc | s: a flier takes off this long before it reaches a bridge at its pace, so it is up over the gap. |

## boki_forms (`content/rules/boki_forms.json`)

Second forms of a Boki (docs/boki/GEODEMOLE_FORMS.md). A Boki with an entry here shows its 'cracked' look instead of its base look while its health is below damaged_below (fraction of max) in a match, or while it is sick at home. Same Boki, same stats: a look swap only. 'art' names the approved 2D art; 'model' is the 3D model file, empty until it exists, and then the base look is used for both forms.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| damaged_below | 0.4 |
| forms | {"geodemole": {"base": {"art": "geodemole-3-art", "model": ""}, "cracked": {"art": "geodemole-r-3-art", "model": ""}}} |

## boki_impact (`content/rules/boki_impact.json`)

The impact sound of a Boki's ability hit (BokiImpact, docs/AUDIO.md). Boki types are labels for identity and colour (DECISIONS 11-10, 19 types): each type has ONE impact, ki_<type>, the take set of its cast cue k_<type> (Sfx loads ki_ names from the k_ files, so the impact has its own voice cap and does not eat the cast). Missing file -> the shared hit/crit plays instead. Types not listed use 'default'.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| slots | ["k1", "k2", "zone"] |
| db | {"you": -8.0, "taken": -9.0, "crit_up": 2.0, "other": -14.0} |
| pitch | 1.1 |
| default | normal |
| types | {"normal": "ki_normal", "fire": "ki_fire", "water": "ki_water", "grass": "ki_grass", "spore": "ki_spore", "electric": "ki_electric", "ice": "ki_ice", "rock": "ki_rock", "psychic": "ki_psychic", "flying": "ki_flying", "dragon": "ki_dragon", "dark": "ki_dark", "ghost": "ki_ghost", "poison": "ki_poison", "bug": "ki_bug", "steel": "ki_steel", "fairy": "ki_fairy", "crystal": "ki_crystal", "sound": "ki_sound"} |

## boki_lines (`content/rules/boki_lines.json`)

What Boki say (BokiLines, docs/BOKI_TALK.md). tuning: max_words = the most words in one bubble (punctuation and symbols don't count); act_words = the most words in one action, which a young Boki says after its name; bubble_s = seconds a bubble stays up; cooldown_s = seconds a Boki waits between lines (a trigger marked direct answers something you did and skips the wait); no_repeat = how many of its own last lines a Boki never repeats; min_lines = the fewest general lines a trigger may have; grown_stage = the speech stage (Care.speech) from which a Boki says lines instead of its name. tones = how a young Boki says its name, by feeling ({A} first syllable, {a} lower, {b} second syllable, {F} full name, {f} lower, {U} upper; KinSpeak.fill). sounds = noises a tone may use besides the name. alias = old trigger names that share another's lines. triggers: feel (a tone), word (the one word a stage-1 Boki adds), acts (what it does), lines._ (anyone) and lines.<element> (extra lines for a Boki of that element, the species' type).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| tuning | {"max_words": 6, "act_words": 4, "bubble_s": 2.0, "cooldown_s": 6.0, "no_repeat": 10, "min_lines": 8, "grown_stage": 2} |
| tones | {"happy": ["{A}! {A}-{a}!", "{F}! {F}!", "{A}-{a}! {F}!", "{F}\u266a", "{A}-{a}-{a}!"], "excited": ["{F}!!", "{A}! {A}! {A}!", "{U}!!", "{A}-{A}-{A}!", "{A}-{b}!!"], "question": ["{A}?", "{F}?", "{a}... {A}?", "{A}-{a}?", "{F}... {f}?"], "sad": ["{a}... {f}...", "{A}...", "{f}...", "{a}... {a}...", "{b}..."], "angry": ["{U}!", "{A}! {A} {A}!!", "Grrr... {A}!", "{A}! {U}!", "Hmph! {A}!"], "sleepy": ["{f}... {b}...", "{A}... zzz...", "{a}-{a}... {f}...", "{b}... {b}...", "Mm... {a}..."], "scared": ["{A}?! {A}!", "{F}...!", "Eep! {A}!", "{a}-{a}-{a}!", "{U}?!"], "love": ["{F}~ \u2665", "{a}-{a}~", "{F}... \u2665", "{A}~ {A}~", "{a}-{b}~ \u2665"], "content": ["{A}.", "{F}.", "{a}-{a}.", "{F}, {a}.", "{A}~"], "refuse": ["{A}. {A}.", "{A}! {A}!", "{U}. {A}.", "{U}! {U}!", "Hmph. {A}."]} |

## boki_modes (`content/rules/boki_modes.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| _doc | Where every Boki line is found (docs/design/SERIES_BOKI_MODES.md, BokiModes). Each line (keyed by its Bokidex base form; kin = the game's species id when the game has it) lives in exactly one mode, with a rarity and the lowest difficulty of that mode it turns up at. tickets: how many draw tickets one species of a rarity gets (a very rare one is 6x less likely than a common one). modes.<id>.sites: which rarities each spawn site of that mode draws from; difficulties: the mode's difficulty ladder, easiest first; future: a reserved slot for a mode not built yet. |
| tickets | {"common": 6, "rare": 3, "very_rare": 1} |
| modes | {"expedition": {"name": "Expeditions", "difficulties": ["normal"], "sites": {"wild": ["common", "rare"], "rare_spot": ["rare", "very_rare"]}}, "heart_raid": {"name": "Heart Raid", "difficulties": ["normal", "hard", "nightmare"]}, "farm": {"name": "The farm", "difficulties": ["normal"]}, "tutorial": {"name": "Tutorial", "difficulties": ["normal"]}, "tidewatch": {"name": "Tidewatch", "future": true, "difficulties": ["normal"]}, "blightdeep": {"name": "Blightdeep", "future": true, "difficulties": ["normal"]}, "skyrun": {"name": "Skyrun", "future": true, "difficulties": ["normal"]}} |

|---|---|
| _doc | Species field-note details (Bokidex quirks-v1, owner 11-09). Keys are Bokidex ids: a game species' display name in lower case (BokiQuirks.key). 'quirk' and 'sexNote' are copied verbatim from bokidex/work/quirks-v1.json; the sections after them make a few of those notes real on the farm. |
| quirk | {"geyserbara": "Erupts on a schedule to the minute; farmers set their clocks by it.", "thundrich": "A small cloud gathers over its head when cross; clear sky means content.", "vatmander": "Its tower fills in rain and the whole farm drinks from it in drought.", "shinobant": "Leaves exactly one cut leaf behind wherever it has slipped past.", "gravidon": "Drops its ring of floating stones in a neat circle before it lies down to sleep.", "harpwhal": "Swims up beside small boats and nudges them gently onto its own course.", "duskspire": "Turns only its eyestalks to follow passers-by and never shows the rest of itself.", "glombulus": "Settles on top of spilled food and simply stays there until it is gone.", "effigoon": "Ticks faintly inside its cocoon on still nights, like a slow clock.", "crofthollow": "Walks extra slowly through autumn fields so the sparrows can keep up with the falling grain.", "citadoad": "Plants itself in the yard gate and lets smaller Boki file past under its chin.", "magnestaff": "Stands at crossroads so still that people hang their hats on it.", "glowris": "Waits all night at crossroads with its lanterns lit until the last walker is home.", "mosstodon": "Lets children climb all over it and only shifts when one is about to fall.", "murmuron": "Breaks into a flock of tiny birds on take-off and gathers itself back up to land.", "strobolin": "Balances a mirror ball on each tail and sets them both down carefully before it eats.", "rimefang": "Can fast for a week but still checks the pantry door every evening.", "lunarca": "Swims slowly between the islands on clear nights and dims its light for nobody.", "barostorm": "Swings its arrow tail round to point at whatever weather is coming next.", "pipeworth": "Pipes a line of sticky icing along every fence it walks beside.", "vespyx": "Hunts at dusk and buries spare prey in shallow scrapes, then forgets half of them.", "vespox": "Wipes its sting on bark every dawn; the scratched trees mark its patrol route.", "glaivyx": "Sleeps standing with the scythe tail raised; nothing wild roosts within a stone's throw.", "prismander": "Keep it by a window: its crystal frills grow faster in direct sunlight.", "glassolotl": "Chirps whenever a rainbow shows, often minutes before anyone else spots it.", "chandelotl": "Its gill crown dims when it sulks and blazes after a bite of sugar cane.", "mycroll": "Rolls through compost after rain; it will not let you polish them.", "kayak": "Paddles across puddles on its back for fun and refuses to come out.", "prowyak": "Clears a path to your door after every snowfall without being asked.", "dreadnoyak": "Breathes frost on hot days to cool itself; the old ones can be traded.", "gloamshell": "Lanterns burn dimmer wherever it crawls; keep it out of the barn at night.", "glomwort": "Creeps toward spilled food overnight; sweep up or wake to a yellow net.", "effigeetle": "Will not fly in rain; ## camps (`content/rules/camps.json`)

| _doc | Monster camps (scripts/match/camps.gd, docs/CAMPS.md). Every camp spot on the map is one of three sizes by its layout kind: light = Small Camp, normal = Camp, heavy = Great Camp. lvl: the level a bot wants before it goes for the camp (bots farm small camps first). n and big: monsters in a camp from a region table, and the one big monster a Great Camp always has. fixed: the monsters of a Great Camp with no region table. A camp's monsters are picked by a dice seeded from its spot alone, so the same camp holds the same monsters every match. back_s: a cleared camp comes back once this many seconds after its clear, if no Hunter is within back_clear_r metres (rolling sessions only). spread: how far (m) the monsters stand from the camp's centre. |

Raising a Boki at home (scripts/core/care.gd). natural_death: false means neglect never kills (owner 2026-11-08): a Boki left unfed bottoms out at sick, then recovers with care. Other losses (expeditions, the Black Market) are unchanged.

| sulky | {"food": 8.0, "energy": 8.0, "joy": 12.0, "clean": 8.0} |
| sulky_doc | base_mode only (GARDEN.md section 2): needs bottom out here, sulky, and the starve clock never builds, so a Boki left alone is never weak or sick. It gets hungry and glum, and feeds itself from a bowl or a snack (BaseFeed). Off base_mode the starve stages apply. |

| care_day_s | 300 |
| care_day_s_doc | Seconds before the same kind of care (petting, fetch, a meal, a chat, training) builds trust again: one farm day (home.gd DAY_LEN). Before 11-09 it was once per expedition, so a Boki raised only at home stopped growing closer. |

| stat_budget_doc | grow_max: extra body size at the full total_cap (StatBudget.growth, read by Evo.dress as evo_scale), 0.12 = 12% taller; it follows the square root of total/total_cap, so 60 points already show 6%. Caps and diminishing gains for the four stats (StatBudget, decision 0022). A stat's cap is min(cap_max, cap_base + cap_per_level x level); the four together stop at total_cap. bands: [last point of the band, share of each gain that counts]. loose_rate: points a respec set loose come back this many a gain, ignoring bands. expedition_stat_points: match_mods reads at most this many points of each stat; minigames read all. |

Carry passive amounts x (1 + score x carry_max); summon window x (1 + score x summon_max). The carry passive still stops at its per-stat carry cap (KinParts.OWNER_STATS), so this never lifts a Boki past the cap a wild one has. |

## class_unlock (`content/rules/class_unlock.json`)

Hunter unlocks and mastery (docs/decisions/0005). A new save picks one of `starters` (Lace, Kael or Vex) on the first-Relic screen, wears it at the first portal and plays the tutorial as it; the Hunter pickers tag the three `starters` with a "Start here" chip until the save has played `start_here_matches` matches. After its first finished expedition the player picks one of `second_picks` as the second Relic (the one already taken is not offered); a starter not taken and not in `second_picks` opens at that same moment. Every other Hunter opens through its own challenge in `unlock`, counted across all your expeditions whoever you play; a challenge with `after` also waits until that many Hunters are open. A done challenge never opens a Hunter by itself: the player holds the button on the Hunters screen for `hold_s` seconds. `mastery` lists each Hunter's goals, counted only in expeditions played as that Hunter; each one done is a mastery level and a cosmetic reward. Rewards are cosmetic only (`reward_kinds`). Ids are Hunter ids, never display names. Every number is a placeholder until the owner tunes it. `looks` are features a Hunter leaves on your own character at home once its mastery reaches `level` (shape `eyes` or `scar`, colour `col`); the creator keeps or fades each (MasteryLook).

| doc | What tools/clip_cadence_check.gd holds each warden_anim clip to. Per art name, per move: 'cadence' = the shortest time before the move is played again or another one replaces it, and 'hit' = when the kit's hit/release lands after the move starts (omitted: the kit has no timed hit, only the cadence is checked), 'hand' = the bone whose fastest frame is the strike (default hand.R). Each is seconds, or 'file:path' into content/ (a list is summed), so a kit number that changes is read from its own json. Moves that loop (hold_from), or whose cooldown is longer than any clip, are not listed. |

## combat (`content/rules/combat.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| doc | The one 'in combat' rule (scripts/match/in_combat.gd). A Hunter or a Boki is in combat for window_s seconds after it deals or takes damage in a fight: a hit on or from a Hunter, a Boki, a monster or Blight. Healing, falls, wall slams, heat, friendly fire and damage to yourself don't count. A Boki's fight is its owner's too. Hunter shield refill, a Boki's own mending, the drive music, a Boki's 10 Hz think out of combat and a Boki's refused orders all read it, so they switch on the same frame. (Far bots' 20 Hz step is SimLod's, not this window: far fights are slowed on purpose.) The source publishes no combat timer [gap]: 5 s is the old Hunter regen wait, kept as the one shared value. Channels (a recall, an exit call, a rune, a box revive) are not on this window: the source cancels them on the hit itself, so they read Hunter.hurt_at. |
| window_s | 5 |

## dash_feel (`content/rules/dash_feel.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| doc | Dash feel (Shift) on top of each kit's own numbers in content/archetypes. dist: multiplier on distance. time: multiplier on duration (speed = dist / time). Parity first (DECISIONS 2026-11-07): a kit whose dash numbers are the source's measured dash runs them as-is (the default, 1.0 / 1.0): Vex, Hem, Cinder, Pip, Bjorn and Sable. Owner, Nov 2: dashes were too fast and too far in general, Sparkle's (Ryzz, mage) should go further. That rule stays only on the kits whose dash has no source number: Zedran's Rampage (owner 113.8), Grimble's Barge (owner 23:40) and Tarek's Rock Hop (owner item 111) at x0.85 distance, x1.15 time; Ryzz's Wirerun lane is the owner's own (item 70), so only its time is scaled. Claire's Skate and Ostra's Lantern Trade never pass through it. moves (optional): the feel per Shift move, by the name the kit passes to travel() ({"feel": name}): a move on a x1 kit with no source figure of its own still runs the owner's x0.85 / x1.15 (Albert's Shield Charge, wind-up short dash and lumber; the class long dash out of charges for Vex, Lace (her flick), Sparkle, Sable and Gil); the hunter's dist and time cover every other move. A long dash runs the class's ex_dist / ex_time (Hunter.dash_with) times its move's feel, so Kael's and Tenzo's long dashes pass "long" too and get their hunter's x0.85 / x1.15. The felt table is asserted in --move-feel-check (docs/KIT_PARITY.md gap 4). Gil runs his own numbers (x1). curve (optional): the hero's measured ground dash speed over the dash, [u, k] knots, u = share of the dash's time, k = speed against the dash's mean (mean 1, so the distance holds), fitted to the hero-ref frame tracks (sv/FEEL_NOTES.md, docs/decisions/0025); the dash then hands over through HunterMove.dash_exit. Heroes with no curve dash at a constant speed. thief's curve is her Cartwheel, on the ground and from a jump (the air one then carries on under air drag to the landing); bulwark's is the 360 Smash only. dolm has none: its Rock Hop is a leap (owner item 111) and the footage's only ground dash is a push it does not have; Claire's Skate is held, so its start is her own dash.ramp (fitted, docs/KIT_PARITY.md gap 4). |

## evolve (`content/rules/evolve.json`)

Evolution (scripts/core/evo.gd). Each entry is a Boki species id and what it evolves into. 'level': the level it evolves at (a level-up at or past it). 'into': the options; 'path' picks a branch by the Boki's leading affinity (fierce/steadfast/curious/swift; one name or a list of names), 'trait' needs that rare trait on the Boki (BokiQuirks, rolled at hatch; it wins over the plain options), 'item' needs that Ink used on it (any level), 'trade' needs it traded to another player. Ids that have no data yet are the owner's roster names in lower case. A Boki never evolves into a species without data and a model (art/kin/<id>/<id>.glb and a BokiRig FRAME row); it waits, and evolves once the art exists.

## farm_build (`content/rules/farm_build.json`)

The farm building pass (docs/decisions/0004-farm-building.md). Farm level is points from play; items unlock by farm level or a milestone; new buildings are construction sites that you hammer (hold interact) and your Boki help build; the materials are spent a quarter at a time as the work goes; buildings upgrade L1 to L3. Units: gems and materials are counts, labour is work swings (one hammer beat of yours is 0.8 s, one swing of a Boki is about 3 s at building skill 1).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| base_mode | True |
| base_mode_doc | On for every player (owner 11-18: the Chao-style garden core is the default home; the home code stays ready for more than one zone, see homes-zones-spec-1118). GARDEN.md section 8: true shrinks the farm to the Boki base. Build mode shows only Buildings, Garden and Island; no axe, pickaxe or wild chopping; no work stations, wild or haul jobs (Boki knacks still run the plot, mend and incubator chores); no Exchange, Sell tab, tools or crop-chain goods at the market; meals lean a Boki by the food's type (content/rules/lean.json, Lean) instead of the four affinities. Nothing is deleted: false changes nothing, and saves are untouched either way. |
| points | {"extracts": 3.0, "bosses": 6.0, "caught": 2.0, "hatched": 2.0, "harvested": 0.25, "built": 2.0, "fb_built": 2.0} |
| points_doc | Farm points = sum(stat * weight). 'built' counts the lot buildings you built, 'fb_built' the buildings Boki finished on the farm. |
| levels | [0, 6, 16, 30, 48, 70] |
| levels_doc | Points needed for farm level 1..6 (index 0 is level 1). |
| milestones | {"first_run": {"name": "First expedition", "stat": "matches", "n": 1, "text": "Go on your first expedition"}, "first_extract": {"name": "First extraction", "stat": "extracts", "n": 1, "text": "Make it out of an expedition once"}, "first_boss": {"name": "First boss", "stat": "bosses", "n": 1, "text": "Defeat a boss in a lair"}, "scan3": {"name": "Three scanned", "stat": "caught", "n": 3, "text": "Scan and bring home 3 wild Boki"}} |
| water | {"reach": 2, "grow": 1.25, "doc": "FarmWater, docs/FARM_LOOP.md. reach: tiles (1 tile = 1 m) from a patch's or trough's footprint to a pond, painted river or wild water tile. grow: growth-speed multiplier for a patch in reach (stage time / grow). A trough in reach tops itself up from the pantry like a hopper."} |
| lots | {"board": {"wood": 6, "stone": 4}} |
| lots_doc | Wood and stone a building LOT costs on a farm under the building pass, instead of its gem price in Data.BUILDINGS (the Challenge House: Hob draws it up after the first expedition). |
| lot_labour | 8 |
| lot_labour_doc | Swings of labour a lot building takes (the Workshop, Cottage, Gear Shed...); its cost is the 'lots' row or its gem price. A lot goes up as a construction site like every other building (FarmLots). |
| starter | ["crop_patch", "cook_pot"] |
| starter_doc | Placed at once, no site. The house is not here: it goes up as a site you and your Boki build (build.house): 10 wood and 6 stone, spent as it goes up. |
| start_doc | What Hob offers from the first minute is every item with no entry in unlock: house, crop_patch, cook_pot, ranch_pen, fence, path_dirt, flowers (and the feeder in storage). Everything in unlock opens by farm level or milestone and is then drawn up when you talk to Hob (scripts/home/farm_builder.gd). |

## farm_builder (`content/rules/farm_builder.json`)

Hob Brackenridge, the farm's builder (docs/decisions/0104-farm-builder-tutorial.md). He stands by the market stall (and works at the house while it goes up); walk up and press interact to talk face to face ('talk'). Blueprints with a level or milestone in farm_build.json unlock for real only once Hob has drawn them up, so a level-up or milestone makes a 'new blueprints' toast and a mark over his head. Everything with no entry there is on offer from the start.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| name | Hob Brackenridge |
| short | Hob |
| stand | {"along": 2.4, "side": 4.2, "desc": "Metres in front of the house centre and to its right, so he never blocks the door (where he works while it is a site)."} |
| stall_stand | {"out": 1.6, "side": 2.2, "desc": "Metres out in front of the market stall and to its side: where his home spot is first looked for (HobSpot)."} |
| clear | {"m": 3.5, "reach_m": 1.9, "desc": "Metres: the clear ring round Hob's home spot. No placed tile, door or other place you interact with comes closer, and build mode refuses a piece inside it. When his spot is chosen, places you interact with are also kept talk_reach + reach_m (the usual 1.9 m interact reach) away, so his talk ring and theirs do not overlap and the talk camera has open ground."} |
| walk_mps | 2.4 |
| swing_s | 6 |
| swing_doc | s between his own swings at a house site; with no materials he waits and says wait_line. |
| wait_line | Can't hammer yet: the house {need}. |
| talk_reach | 2.4 |
| hint_more | Talk to Hob for more |
| toast | New blueprints: talk to Hob |

| menu_hint_empty | Hob has nothing new for you yet. |

## farm_tutorial (`content/rules/farm_tutorial.json`)

The guided farm tutorial (state: Save.d.tutorial.ft = {did, done, skipped}). Short, one prompt at a time, always with a visible Skip (owner, Nov 8 DECISIONS.md: a skipped player still gets the house, the tools and the starter food). Every owner-confirmable choice is under 'options' so it is a one-line change.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| options | {"tracker_replaces_day1": true, "player_swing": true, "crop_stage_s": 6, "end_gems": 30, "skippable": true, "house_cost_in": "farm_build.json build.house (wood and stone, spent as it goes up, and swings of labour)", "free_order": true, "free_tools": true, "market_gems": true} |
| options_doc | tracker_replaces_day1: the top-right card is the Goals tracker. player_swing: holding the interact key near a site hammers (hold it: a hammer beat every HunterTool.TOOLS.hammer.period seconds), so one Boki is enough. end_gems: the one reward at the end (the old +5 each and +30). free_order: after the house is down feed, crop and the rest can come in any order (meeting Hob comes first: he calls you over) (false: strictly in the listed order). skippable: shows a Skip button (the owner wants it always there). free_tools: a step with gives_tool hands that tool over (the axe, the pickaxe); the Market still sells them later. market_gems: the buy step tops the gems up to one seed's price so nobody gets stuck. |
| house_spot | {"from": "landing", "x": 0.0, "z": -7.0} |
| start_food | {"kibble": 3} |
| build_wait_s | 30 |
| site_hint | Boki build it while you are home: a run pauses the work until you are back. |

| base | {"doc": "The Boki base's tutorial (GARDEN.md section 8; only while farm_build.json base_mode is on, then it replaces 'steps'): meet your Boki, plant the snack patch, feed it and watch it change, place a toy and watch it play, head out or stay. One banner line each, a Skip that leaves a toy placed and food in hand. start_food: a typed food, so the feed step shows the lean change. skip_toy: the toy put down on a skip. near: tiles from your Boki that count as meeting it. lead: your Boki leads each step (scripts/home/base_tut_lead.gd): it waits and looks back when you are more than wait_m metres behind, and stops stop_m metres short of the place. boki: the line it says over its head when the step comes up.", "lead": {"wait_m": 6.0, "stop_m": 1.8}, "start_food": {"emberberry": 3}, "skip_toy": "toy_ball", "near": 3.0, "steps": [{"id": "meet", "title": "Meet your Boki", "hints": {"go": "This is your Boki. It is free and grows the snacks that feed your Boki."}, "world": {"go": ""}, "spot": {"go": {"hub": "build", "tile": "snack_patch", "tab": "Garden"}}, "boki": "Can we grow some snacks?"}, {"id": "eat", "needs": ["patch"], "title": "Feed it", "hints": {"go": "Click your Boki (or press {details} next to it), choose Feed and give it the {food}: watch its colour change."}, "world": {"go": "Feed your Boki"}, "boki": "Is that a berry? | first_day | {"reward_gems": 15, "start_items": {"kibble": 2}, "doc": "A new save gets this short list in the Goals tracker (GardenFirstDay): one line each, ticked as the thing happens, one small gem reward when the last is ticked, then it is gone. Not tutorial steps. Saves made before it have no 'gfd' state and never see it. start_items: what a new save's bag holds besides the tonic, so 'Feed your Boki' has food from the first frame (the tutorial's own feed step adds more later). needs_grown: the row shows only once a Boki in the roster is Grown (NookRules.GROWN_LV, level 8), because pairing needs it and a new player cannot do it on day one; a ticked row still shows.", "rows": [{"id": "feed", "text": "Feed your Boki"}, {"id": "toy", "text": "Play with a toy"}, {"id": "race", "text": "Run your first race"}, {"id": "nap", "text": "See a nap pile", "two": true}, {"id": "pair", "text": "Pair two Boki in the Nook", "two": true, "needs_grown": true}]} |

| steps_doc | needs: steps that must be done first; needs_all: everything else; after_built: the house must stand; waits: hint stages that are only waiting (the next open step is shown meanwhile); gives_tool: handed over when the step comes up; gets: a material that finishes the step (detect); spot: per hint stage, what FarmSpotlight lights up (hub: a bottom-bar button id, world: the step's marker in the world, a Boki; tile + tab: the build-bar entry to pick once build mode is open, or its tab). Each target gets its full dimmed beat once, then only a soft ring. |

## first_match_guide (`content/rules/first_match_guide.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| doc | The first-match guide (scripts/match/first_match_guide.gd): one plain 'what to do next' line at a time in the first two real Extractions of a save. matches: how many Extractions get it. gap: seconds of quiet between two lines. close_at: the part of the match left when the Blight line shows. lines: [id, text, longest it stays in seconds]; the zone and wall lines show once per profile (Save tutorial guide_zone, guide_wall), the others once a match. dive_open_s: seconds with the glider open, and dive_height: metres above the ground, before the dive line shows (once per save, Save.d tutorial glide_dive, in any Extraction). In the text %C is the crouch key (the dive), %F is the interact key, %T the Boki key, %R the rank-up keys, %N the ability's name, %B the base-to-a-teammate key, %s the Boki's name, %X the way out ExtractGoal points at (its map badge) and %H how to use it (exit_none when no way out is on offer). mates_far: metres from every teammate at which the B line shows (it also shows after the squad line). |
| matches | 2 |
| gap | 1.5 |
| close_at | 0.4 |
| mates_far | 30 |
| exit_none | Go to an exit and hold %F to leave |
| dive_open_s | 1.5 |
| dive_height | 15 |
| lines | [["chest", "Loot a chest: stand next to it and hold %F", 25.0], ["rank", "Rank up %N: press %R", 20.0], ["send", "Send %s at a monster: tap %T", 20.0], ["zone", "Stay in the blue ring on your minimap: outside it you lose health over time", 14.0], ["wall", "You are outside the zone and losing health: run for the blue ring", 12.0], ["mates", "Hold %B to pick a teammate, release to teleport. Takes 5 s; taking damage cancels it.", 14.0], ["blight", "The Blight is closing in: time to wrap up", 12.0], ["exit", "Head for the %X badge on your map: %H", 40.0], ["dive", "Gliding: hold %C to dive", 12.0]] |

## garden_daily (`content/rules/garden_daily.json`)

The garden's daily hooks (scripts/home/garden_wishes.gd, scripts/home/garden_away.gd; briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 5, ranks 1 and 3). Each garden day three Boki wish for something (a need back up); granting one is a gift, nothing is ever taken for missing a day. Coming back after time away brings small gifts. Nothing here lowers a need or a stat.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| day_s | 86400 |
| day_s_doc | Seconds in one garden day (the local calendar day, cut at midnight). |
| wishes | {"count": 3, "count_doc": "Wishes picked each garden day, one card.", "needs": ["food", "energy", "clean", "joy"], "needs_doc": "The needs a wish can be for (the same four KinWants shows as thought bubbles).", "pick_below": 60.0, "pick_below_doc": "A Boki is only picked for a need that is under this (0 to 100), so a wish always has something to do.", "wish_to": 80.0, "wish_to_doc": "The wish is granted when that need is back at or above this (0 to 100), however it got there: you, a toy, a feeder.", "trust": 2.0, "trust_doc": "Trust points (0 to 100) the Boki gains when its wish is granted.", "item": "kibble", "item_n": 1, "item_doc": "The small item a granted wish puts in the pantry (Save.d items).", "bonus_gems": 6, "bonus_doc": "Gems for all the wishes of the day (the Sunsap of GARDEN_MODERN.md 1.2 stands in until the item engine is merged).", "tip": "Grant one for trust and a snack; all %d give %d gems. Miss a day and nothing is lost.", "ask": {"food": "%s is hungry for a meal", "energy": "%s would love a nap", "clean": "%s wants a wash", "joy": "%s wants some fun"}} |
| away | {"gift_every_h": 2.0, "gift_every_h_doc": "Hours away for each small gift a Boki saves you (a snack of its leading lean).", "gift_max": 3, "gift_max_doc": "Most gifts on one return (so 6 hours away fills it).", "toy_rate": 0.25, "toy_rate_doc": "Share of the at-home training speed toys keep while you are away.", "toy_cycle_s": 90.0, "toy_cycle_s_doc": "Seconds one stat point takes at a toy while you are home (play time plus the walk to it).", "toy_cap": 3, "toy_cap_doc": "Most stat points one Boki trains on one return, never past its level cap.", "patch_overflow_max": 3, "patch_overflow_max_doc": "Most extra snack-patch batches (beyond the one that waits on the patch) that go to the feeder bowl on one return."} |

## garden_items (`content/rules/garden_items.json`)

Shaping items (scripts/core/garden_items.gd; design briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 1). They live in the garden bag (Save.d items), are fed from a Boki's feed menu, and always show their exact effect (no 'Effect: ?' rule). Effects: stat = +n to one Care.STATS stat up to its cap; xp = +n xp (levels and forms follow); token = a worn path token for the aff (rec.path, at most max_tokens, take_off returns it to the bag); stay = worn Stayleaf (rec.stay); rinse = clear rec.lean; loose = up to n points out of the Boki's highest stat into rec.loose; stat_all = +n to all four stats (up to the level cap); sweet = the picked type among types jumps to share of Evo.LEAN_FULL and holds (rec.hold, hold_days garden days, no fade from other meals); trait = a trait moves by (signed), counted in base_drift week_cap (rec.drift.moved); twin = shared by two Boki: trait by on each and bond between them. sources are where the item comes from; desc (nest items only) is the plain line under the item's row in the feed menu; this file does not drop them, except lair_drop below. aura = a worn look, one at a time (rec.aura; its aura block is drawn by GardenAura, scripts/home/garden_aura.gd: night_only glows after dark, lean takes the Boki's lean colour, chime puffs notes when HomeChimes hears it happy or winning; one particle set, none at low quality). Nest items (scripts/core/nest_items.gd) are placed in the Nesting Nook with a pair and used up when the egg is laid: nest gifts = n more inborn gifts from the parents per Thread (at most max Threads); species = the baby is the species of the parent wearing it; habit = the baby takes that parent's habit and strongest trait exactly. down = trust +trust and a memory line (one drops at every hatch).

## garden_prizes (`content/rules/garden_prizes.json`)

Garden minigame prizes and weekly cups (scripts/home/garden_prizes.gd; briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 4.4). Each game has a weighted prize table (one roll for the backed Boki's win), a guaranteed first-win-of-the-day item, and a cup of three wins in a row against stronger rivals (cup.rounds). Winning the last round (Crown) gives the game's Cup Ribbon to the winning Boki (rec.ribbons) and the cup prize; one Crown per game per week per Boki. Table entries: kind item = a shaping item id in garden_items.json (banked in Save.d items), kind snack = a Data.CROPS food (banked in Save.d crops). A game may name a first_crown item: a Boki's first Crown in that game also banks it (Echo Steps: Chimegrass).

## garden_recipes (`content/rules/garden_recipes.json`)

The Mixing Bowl's six recipes (scripts/core/garden_recipes.gd, screen scripts/ui/mixing_bowl.gd; GARDEN_MODERN.md 1.4). All are listed from the start and none can fail: the bowl shows what it will take and what comes out before you confirm. need.kind: different = n different items out of 'of' (one each); snack_type = n snacks (Save.d crops) that all share one lean type out of 'types' (Lean.key_of); same = n of one item. gives is a garden_items id; n how many come out. tier 1-3 is how grand the finished chime is (BowlSfx).

## garden_seasons (`content/rules/garden_seasons.json`)

Garden seasons (scripts/home/garden_seasons.gd; briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 5 rank 9). Every few weeks one zone is in season, in list order, counted on the weekly-event clock (BaseRace.week_now, the device clock the save uses; no server). While in season: the zone's game plays its season twist (unless this week's weekly format is already for that game), the snack patch grows the season's snack on top of its four, and that game's Crown also gives the season's keepsake (rec.keepsakes, once a season per Boki).

## garden_sim (`content/rules/garden_sim.json`)

Inputs for tools/garden_sim.py, the headless 30-day garden balance sim (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN_BALANCE.md). The sim reads the live rules where they exist (care.json stat_budget, garden_prizes.json, garden_items.json, evo_paths.json) and falls back to the copies under fallback, taken from the READY branches ext/garden-stat-budget 7d1acb8c6, ext/garden-prizes-cups 9f2fdb16f and ext/garden-path-meter c1275d53a. Garden XP (GARDEN_MODERN 2.5) is not built anywhere yet, so garden_xp is the brief's numbers. Everything marked assume is a sim guess, not a game rule.

| bands_doc | Target bands, [low, high], every player must land inside (docs/GARDEN.md Balance). form_lv4_day: median day of the first form step (Evo.on_level, level 4, 600 XP); evolution_day: median day of the first real form swap (first_evo_level) on garden XP alone, so a home-only player still evolves (DECISIONS 2026-11-09); budget_full_day: when the 240 budget fills (only checked where it fills inside the month: never trivial); stat_total: total at the end of the month (90% of 240 or more: even five minutes a day nearly fills it); gems_day: mean gems earned a day (at least a weekly Wayseed, 300 / 7, so home-only players reach every zone; at most one a day); joy: mean joy over a visit (above sulky, below always full so toys and cares still matter). |

## garden_trust (`content/rules/garden_trust.json`)

Trust from care at the base (Care.trust_up). Petting, its habit food and winning together each raise trust by a named amount, shown to the player as one plain line. Trust stays 0 to 100 and nothing here lowers it. A habit (rec.habit.food) is picked when a Boki hatches, from its element (the species theme).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| pet | 1 |
| food | 2 |
| win | 3 |
| taper | {"free": 6, "step": 0.35, "floor": 0.05} |
| taper_doc | Per-Boki daily taper on every trust gain (Care.trust_add: pets, habit food, wins, fetch, chats, hand feeding, minigame wins). The first free paid acts in a window (care.json care_day_s, opened by the first act) pay in full; act free+n pays 1 - step x n of its amount, never under floor. The window resets when care_day_s has passed, so a new garden day pays in full again. |
| cooldown_h | 1 |
| hour_s | 12.5 |
| say | {"pet": "%s loved the scratches: trust up", "food": "%s loves %s: trust up", "win": "%s won with you: trust up"} |
| default_food | kibble |
| food_by_element | {"ember": "emberberry", "frost": "frostdrop", "bloom": "puffcorn", "storm": "tonicbrew", "stone": "pebblenut", "gravity": "ironcrisp", "titan": "scalepepper", "shadow": "duskplum", "lunar": "mindmint", "venom": "pricklepear", "echo": "chimebun", "prism": "geodecandy", "spore": "glowcap", "swarm": "sapjelly", "tempest": "tonicbrew"} |
| _units | pet, food, win: trust points (0 to 100). cooldown_h: in-game hours between two raises of one kind on one Boki. hour_s: real seconds in one in-game hour (the home day is 300 s, so 300 / 24). |

## garden_visitor (`content/rules/garden_visitor.json`)

Wild visitors (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 5 rank 6; scripts/home/garden_visitor.gd). While you are in a zone, every check_s seconds of farm time and with no visitor and none due to wait, a wild Boki may wander in: one of the common species that has a rigged model, whose theme is in the zone's group, when the zone has a toy it likes (toys.json likes) and at least residents of the group living there. It stays one garden day (care.json care_day_s), plays your games as one more Boki, and eats only what you hand it. feeds meals of its favourite make it leave an egg (or, with room in the zone, ask to stay as a new Boki). Save.d visitor = {rec, zone, t, fed, notes, next, lead}; intro: the first visitor on a save is led to by your partner with one tip (scripts/home/visitor_intro.gd), a lazy key with no save bump.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| check_s | 60 |
| check_s_doc | Seconds of farm time between looks at whether a visitor comes. |
| chance | 0.3 |
| chance_doc | Chance a look brings a visitor when the zone suits one: about one every three minutes in a zone that does. |
| residents | 2 |
| residents_doc | Residents of the visitor's type group a zone needs. |
| feeds | 3 |
| feeds_doc | Favourite meals it takes before it leaves an egg or asks to stay. |
| gap_s | 300 |
| gap_s_doc | Seconds after one leaves before the next may come (one garden day). |
| intro | {"text": "A wild {name} is visiting {zone} today. Press {interact} on it and hand it {food}, its favourite, three times: it may leave an egg or ask to stay.", "lead_s": 60.0, "lead_s_doc": "Seconds your partner leads you to the first visitor on a save, if you do not walk over first.", "near_m": 3.5, "near_m_doc": "Metres from the visitor at which you count as having come over.", "tip_s": 9.0, "tip_s_doc": "Seconds the tip stays in the message lane."} |
| groups | {"bramblebank": ["bloom", "swarm", "spore"], "glasswater": ["prism", "frost"], "cinderstep": ["ember", "stone", "titan", "gravity"], "hushwood": ["shadow", "lunar", "venom"], "ridge": ["storm", "tempest", "echo"]} |
| arrive | {"prints": 8, "step_m": 0.9, "print_m": 0.16, "alpha": 0.45, "fade_in_s": 2.0, "hold_s": 8.0, "fade_out_s": 3.0, "shimmer_s": 3.0, "mote_s": 0.3, "motes": 3, "glint_s": 2.5} |
| arrive_doc | How a visitor reads as a stranger (scripts/home/visitor_arrive.gd): prints footprints, step_m m apart (print_m m wide, up to alpha opaque), run from the island edge to where it stands, fade in over fade_in_s, hold hold_s and fade out over fade_out_s; a burst of motes sparks of its type colour on it every mote_s seconds for its first shimmer_s seconds; one glint every glint_s seconds on an egg it left, until the egg is hatched. |

## garden_zones (`content/rules/garden_zones.json`)

The garden's hub and zones (briefs/design/GARDEN.md 10; scripts/home/garden_zones.gd, docs/decisions/0120-garden-zones.md). Save.d zones = {id: {open}}, rec zone = the Boki's home zone. zones: name, colour (its stone's glow and card), types (lean.json types; the 18 split five ways), loves (two favoured types and a nature, see affinity), trait (Care trait it matches), game (what its card says is played there), play (its minigames.json id, for your best on the card) and wayseed_from (where the card says the Wayseed comes from); nap: [kind, tile x, tile z] the spots a Boki about to nap walks to, one Boki on each and a friend beside it (BaseLife; a spot moves up to 3 m to open ground, so the start zone's own island keeps them; the hub and zones without an island have none). A zone with a build has its own island (scripts/home/zone_layout.gd, zone_dress.gd): theme (a HomeLayout.THEMES id), seed and sk (the fs island), deco [id, tile x, tile z, quarter turns], shallow [x0, z0, x1, z1] tiles of the channel (only Glasswater has one), clear [x0, z0, x1, z1] tiles kept free of the wild trees and rocks (they are the costliest draws; the scatter dresses the zone instead), scatter (seed, a count per kind: crystal, reed, pebble, terrace, crack; shore = tiles the crystals and reeds crowd the channel), vents [x, z] metres of the updraft vents (scripts/home/zone_vents.gd; only Kitewind Ridge; the first stands on the Dash's track).

|---|---|

## glint_fishing (`content/rules/glint_fishing.json`)

Glint Fishing (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md 4.2 game 4; scripts/home/glint_fishing.gd). Solo with your partner on a rock in a zone that has a spot. Five casts: hold interact to swing the cast out and back, release on a glint, wait, press when your Boki's ears go up, then hold and release to keep the line's tension in the band until the glint is landed. Units: seconds, metres, tension 0-1, stats 0-100 points, joy and trust 0-100.

## hit_flinch (`content/rules/hit_flinch.json`)

How hard a hit flinches a Hunter (Oomph.hit_strength, Oomph.flinch_weight). Strength hit_k = chip_k + damage share of max health * frac_k + knock (m/s) * knock_k, from chip_k up to Oomph.HEAVY_FLINCH; a big hit (stagger) is always the heaviest. The body's spring (HunterAnim) scales by hit_k; the clip hero's base additive flinch layer (WardenClips) plays `light` of the hit clip on a chip hit and all of it by a stagger, which takes the whole body. Source-quality weight: a chip hit never looks like a knockdown, a big one is never a twitch.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| chip_k | 0.8 |
| frac_k | 9 |
| knock_k | 0.06 |

## home_lead (`content/rules/home_lead.json`)

A big Boki led at home (scripts/home/home_carry.gd _lead). It walks at your own pace and speeds up to catch a gap, so it keeps up with the Empty's walk and run (HunterMove speed x carry_speed_k) instead of a fixed pace; its stride follows the speed (BokiRig clip cadence), so the feet keep planted.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| top_k | 1.2 |
| top_k_doc | most its catch-up speeds it past your own speed, as a multiple; 1.2 of a 4.5 m/s lead is 5.4 m/s, the fastest pace --boki-anim-audit checks (HOME_SPEEDS). |
| catch_gain | 1.2 |
| catch_gain_doc | share of your speed it adds per metre it is behind its slot (1/m), up to top_k. |
| back_s | 0.075 |
| back_s_doc | s of your walking it trails behind its side slot: the slot sits your speed x back_s metres behind you (0.3 m at 4 m/s). |

## hunter_move (`content/rules/hunter_move.json`)



| Setting | Value |

| doc | Per-hunter run speed and acceleration [game data]: the reference's character attributes (MoveSpeed uu/s, MaxAcceleration uu/s^2), divided by 100 for metres. Ids are our archetypes: bulwark = Oath, dredge = Kingpin, thief = Shiv, mage = Joule, dolm = Tetra, ostra = Void, ashwick = Felix, juggernaut = Brall, archer = Myth, tender = Elluna, gunslinger = Ghost, rimewright = Celeste. climb_tall: the hunter can mantle double-high ledges (bCanWallJump: Myth and Brall only). A hunter not listed uses the default row. body_scale: our hunters stand taller than the source's, so speed and accel are the row times this, which keeps the source's walk in body heights per second (ours, est). The source hunter is 1.76 m (bot nav agent height 176 uu); ours is 2.04 m (the plain medium hunter at Hunter.VIS_SCALE, --move-feel-check 'model ... tall'); 455 uu/s is 2.59 heights/s; 2.04 / 1.76 = 1.16. The farm, the Training Grounds and an expedition all walk through HunterMove.speed and HunterMove.walk (decision 0061, owner 11-11: same speed everywhere, as fast as the source). The glide cruise and the glide steer force (physics glide_cruise, glide_accel) are scaled by it too, so a run into a glide keeps the source's MaxGlide-to-MoveSpeed ratio (1.03-1.12x) and a glide turn takes the source's time. |

| physics | {"doc": "Ground stop, dash exit, air, fall, glide, dive and mantle tunables shared by every hunter [game data]: the reference hero's movement component and the world settings, uu divided by 100 for metres. brake: BrakingDecelerationWalking (m/s^2), the constant part of the walking stop. ground_friction: GroundFriction (1/s) times braking_friction_factor (UE's BrakingFrictionFactor, default 2) is the share of the speed a let-go sheds per second. braking_substep: UE's BrakingSubStepTime (s, default 1/33): a longer step brakes in sub-steps of at most this. brake_stop_speed: UE's BRAKE_TO_STOP_VELOCITY 10 uu/s (m/s), a brake that leaves less stops dead. min_tick: UE's MIN_TICK_TIME (s), the shortest sub-step braked. Together (UE's ApplyVelocityBraking exactly) a let-go from a run stops in ~0.17 s and 0.31-0.37 m at our 60 Hz step; the source slides 0.28-0.33 m at 30 fps and 0.34-0.39 m at 144 fps (docs/MOVEMENT_PARITY.md). dash_exit_run: a dash ends at this share of run speed (never faster than the dash), so it carries into the walk, brake or jump instead of stopping dead; the data has no hard stop, and the dash curves that set the exact exit are not decoded. Air control is not here: the owner overruled the reference's low AirControl (11-08), see content/rules/tuning.json air. fall_cap: AbyssFallSlowSpeedLimitMin (m/s), the fastest fall, easing to abyss_fall_cap between abyss_slow_from and abyss_slow_to metres under an island's lip over the abyss (AbyssFallSlowDistMin/Max). glide_height: GlideDownwardForceHeightTarget, above which the glider pulls you down at up to glide_pull_vy (GlideDownwardForceMinZVelocity); the pull's extra sink becomes swoop speed on the level-out (tuning.json glide.swoop). glide_cruise: the glide's settled speed, 700 uu/s (m/s: target 800, settles ~700, measured ~720; the old MaxGlide 500 read was the wrong row; item 163 'too fast' was at 6.5 and is an owner question), the cruise for every hunter. glide_accel: GlideTargetXYForce 162,500 over the hunter's Mass 100 (m/s^2), the glider's pull toward where you steer at or under cruise, so a turn or a reversal has inertia (a reversal at cruise ~0.6 s). Both are at body_scale (HunterMove.glide_cruise, HunterMove.glide_accel): 8.12 m/s and 18.85 m/s^2. glide_start_vy / glide_rise_vy / glide_rise_h [game data]: the glider catches a fall the step it opens, at no more than glide_start_vy m/s down whatever the fall, and keeps a rise only up to glide_rise_vy m/s when it opens near the ground, easing to none between glide_rise_h metres up (Loco.glide_start; the canopy then settles to its sink, tuning.json glide.catch). glide_sink [game data]: m/s a glider sinks under glide_height, GlideMinZVelocity -125 uu/s (1.25 m/s; gravity factor 0.025 is -0.37 m/s^2 so the sink cap rules a steady glide; the owner found 2.2 too fast). glide_heat_s: s of a level glide from the open to overheat, the clock every heat cost is a share of (ours: the source coefficients are encrypted; footage ~14 s in Tom Kick's guide, cut to 9 by the owner, 11-02: \"lasts too long, not punishing enough\"; per hunter x archetype glide_cap). turn_rate: RotationRate yaw (deg/s), how fast the body turns to the cursor: a fixed rate, so a small aim change lands at once and a 180 takes 0.14 s. Each ability plays in its own clip (AbilityClip): the real model uses it on a training dummy. `moves`: per Hunter and slot, the kit moves (any kit move table, HunterAnim.km_def) played back to back in the clip, the same ids the kits play. ## impact_weight (`content/rules/impact_weight.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| _doc | Hit weight (docs/DASHES_AND_ABILITY_FEEL.md §5.4): three tiers with a fixed hit-stop and shake, the tier of every Hunter ability, and the stacking caps that keep a team fight readable. hitstop_ms: how long the struck body holds (and the attacker too on a melee hit when attacker is true). The shake of each tier is its <tier>_hit class in content/rules/shake.json (the struck player's camera only; only heavy shakes). flash_ms: how long the struck body flashes white (Ent.flash_t; a tick flashes the light one); a kit never sets its own (docs/DASHES_AND_ABILITY_FEEL.md §5.4 hit-feel table). boki: the tier of a summoned Boki's hits (its basic bite, its tagged ability, throw and recall hits). Hunters: arch id -> ability key (lmb, rmb, dash, e, x, or a kit's own hit tag such as rock or fan) -> tier. --impact-weight-check asserts every damaging ability has one. |
| tiers | {"light": {"hitstop_ms": 25, "attacker": false, "flash_ms": 120}, "solid": {"hitstop_ms": 50, "attacker": true, "flash_ms": 120}, "heavy": {"hitstop_ms": 90, "attacker": true, "flash_ms": 120}} |
| cap | {"hitstop_ms": 110, "hitstop_window_s": 0.5, "repeat_s": 0.25, "repeat_k": 0.33, "shake_gap_s": 0.5} |
| boki | {"basic": "light", "ability": "solid"} |
| hunters | {"archer": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "juggernaut": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "heavy", "dash": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "gunslinger": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "bulwark": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "dash": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "ashwick": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "dash": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "tender": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "dolm": {"lmb": "light", "rock": "solid", "rmb": "heavy", "dash": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "dredge": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "dash": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "rimewright": {"lmb": "light", "fan": "light", "passive": "light", "rmb": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "mage": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "dash": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "thief": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "ostra": {"lmb": "light", "rmb": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}, "gil": {"lmb": "light", "passive": "solid", "rmb": "solid", "dash": "solid", "e": "solid", "x": "heavy"}} |

## incubator (`content/rules/incubator.json`)

The Incubator (scripts/core/incubator.gd, decision 0080). An egg in a cradle hatches after hatch_secs of play time: time in the garden and time in a match both count, time with the game closed does not. An Ember kin at the brazier and Ember Coals add to the pace.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| hatch_secs | 1200 |
| hatch_secs_doc | Seconds of play an egg needs at the plain pace (20 minutes). |

## ink_drops (`content/rules/ink_drops.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| doc | Where Inks come from in a match (scripts/match/ink_drops.gd, called from GearDrops.run_table). An Ink is a backpack item (Loot.ink): carry it out and it goes to your goods (Goods, content/rules/market.json 'ink_<type>'), where Boki that evolve by Ink use it (content/rules/evolve.json). Bosses drop the Ink of their kin's type; camp monsters and guards rarely drop a random one. Per expedition, Goods.on_result adds one more small chance (market.json finds.ink). |
| inks | ["ember", "tide", "bloom", "storm", "frost", "shadow", "lunar", "prism", "wyrm"] |
| type_ink_doc | The 18 types (theme ids in content/kin, owner names from DECISIONS 2026-11-08 22:29 in brackets) to the 9 Inks. Nine types have their own Ink. The rest take the nearest in feel: spore and swarm (Bug) are growth, venom (Poison) is dark, tempest (Flying) rides the Wyrm's sky, titan (Steel) is forged in fire, stone (Rock) is cold and old, echo (Sound) is storm, gravity (Psychic) is lunar, wild (Normal) is every colour at once. |
| type_ink | {"ember": "ember", "tide": "tide", "bloom": "bloom", "storm": "storm", "frost": "frost", "shadow": "shadow", "lunar": "lunar", "prism": "prism", "wyrm": "wyrm", "spore": "bloom", "swarm": "bloom", "venom": "shadow", "tempest": "wyrm", "titan": "ember", "stone": "frost", "echo": "storm", "gravity": "lunar", "wild": "prism"} |
| chance_doc | Chance a kill drops one Ink, by drop table (a mob's kind, or 'boss' for a lair boss). Absent = never. A boss always drops its own. The rest are rare on purpose: an Ink is a 60-gem good and a match has about 40 small kills, so the small ones add up to roughly one Ink in ten matches; guards and the Glimmerkin are the few worth hunting for. |
| chance | {"boss": 1.0, "warden": 0.1, "glimmer": 0.1, "brute": 0.03, "sentinel": 0.01, "spitter": 0.003, "bomber": 0.003, "skitter": 0.003} |

## land_feel (`content/rules/land_feel.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| doc | How hard a Hunter's touchdown squashes (HunterAnim.land_tier picks the way down) by weight class (the 'weight' in content/archetypes). hop: a plain jump or a small step down. drop: a terrace drop or a glider let go. dive: the glide dive's plunge. depth: how far the squash goes (1 is the deepest crouch); a drop or a dive deepens with the fall speed up to 1, so theirs is the least. s: seconds from touchdown until the squash is gone. Parity first (DECISIONS 2026-11-07), source = the private footage reads. light: the thief's jump lands in a low crouch held ~0.1 s, then up in ~0.05 s (hop 0.15 s). heavy: the bulwark's slam lands in the deepest squash of the six, a crouch onto the knees, ~0.5 s in a low recovery (drop and dive: depth 1, 0.5 s). The other cells have no footage and keep the numbers the procedural landing ran before this table [est]: medium everywhere, light's drop and dive (medium's shorter by a quarter) and heavy's hop (a quarter longer than medium's). clip: a cell from the footage also holds a Hero's .glb land clip (WardenClips.land_play) for its s, playing the same keys of the clip in that time; the other cells leave the clip on the Hero's own warden_anim land data. Medium: the reads disagree and give no number (the tender's air-dash touchdown has almost no squash, the dolm's reference squashes hard on every landing, the ostra's landing is not shown), so it stays [est]. No burst, ring or disc on landing (DECISIONS). Asserted per class in --land-weight-check. |

## lantern_match (`content/rules/lantern_match.json`)

Lantern Match, a memory game (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md section 4.2 game 6, scripts/home/lantern_match.gd). Only with farm_build.json base_mode on. Twelve glowcaps in a ring flash in pairs, then go dark; open two at a time to find the pairs. Your Boki sniffs every so often and points at the partner of the last cap you opened, if it saw that cap. Solo against the clock, or turn by turn against a Boki. Units: seconds, probabilities 0-1, joy and trust are 0-100 points.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| colours | ["#ffd166", "#7ee0ff", "#c69cff", "#8cf0a0", "#ff8fb1", "#ffa65c"] |
| colours_doc | One glow colour per pair; the ring holds two caps of each (so 12 caps). |
| flash_s | 0.6 |
| flash_doc | When a ring is dealt each pair glows for flash_s seconds in turn, then all go dark; the clock waits while it flashes. |
| time_s | 90 |
| time_doc | The clock in seconds. Versus: whoever holds more pairs when it runs out (or the ring is cleared) wins; a tie is a draw. |
| solo_goal | 18 |
| solo_doc | Solo: a cleared ring deals a fresh one (and flashes again); find solo_goal pairs before the clock runs out to win. |
| reveal_s | 0.9 |
| reveal_doc | Two caps that do not match stay lit this long, then go dark. In versus the turn then passes; a match keeps the turn. |
| sniff_s | 6 |
| sniff_per_focus | 0.02 |
| sniff_curiosity | 1 |
| sniff_doc | Seconds between your Boki's sniffs: sniff_s / ((1 + Focus points * sniff_per_focus) * (1 + (curiosity - 0.5) * sniff_curiosity)), at least sniff_min. 50 Focus sniffs twice as often; a fully curious Boki half as often again. |
| sniff_min | 1 |
| see | 0.4 |
| see_per_focus | 0.008 |
| see_doc | Chance your Boki notices a pair while it flashes: see + Focus points * see_per_focus, at most 1. Every cap opened in play it always sees. |
| foe_mem | 0.45 |
| foe_mem_per_focus | 0.008 |
| foe_mem_doc | Versus: the chance the rival Boki remembers a cap it has seen (in the flash or opened by anyone): foe_mem + its Focus points * foe_mem_per_focus, at most 0.95. |
| foe_s | 0.8 |
| foe_doc | Seconds the rival Boki takes before each cap it opens. |
| energy | 6 |
| win_joy | 10 |
| win_trust | 3 |
| lose_joy | -6 |
| gems | 4 |
| gems_doc | Gems to you when a game ends (win or not). |
| card_s | 6 |

## mantle_look (`content/rules/mantle_look.json`)

The Relic look (docs/decisions/0011-mantle-look.md). In a match a Relic wearer looks like the class's original Hunter (`wardens`: folk, face, hair, palette; the class's gear and silhouette come from the archetype), nudged by the player's own person (Save look, PlayerLook). Each slider (0..1, 0.5 = neutral) moves its model factor by at most `sliders.<key>.clamp` either way (a Hunter's own `clamp` block overrides it); at home the player is their own person, with `own_k` times that range and their own colours. Each colour pick pulls the Hunter's colour `pull` of the way in HSV, never more than `hue` / `sat` / `val` (a Warden's `tint` block overrides it), so signature colours stay. Hitboxes never read any of this. `presets` set the face sliders as a starting point. Gender is the base character's, read from the archetype JSON (OWNER_REVIEW item 39; 'robot' builds on the male body).

## mask_moment (`content/rules/mask_moment.json`)

Putting on a Relic (MaskBeat, scripts/ui/mask_beat.gd): build-up, the Relic rising to the face, a cut to black and silence, the fallen Hunter on grey panels of their painted art (three memories: their past, their fall, the legend, the last held with a whisper; a Hunter without them shows their face, then their pose), the snap back with an impact and a ripple of light, a pose, the name and title, and a sting. Times in seconds. 'full' is the first Mask (and every first time); 'short' is a later Mask on the farm. About 2.3x its first cut, the panels 4-6 s in all (owner 11-11: too fast to read; 'like 5 s, not 1 s'; owner 11-17: they went by in 1-2 s because the farm's first Relic ran the short cut and a click cut it short: now the first Mask anywhere is the full cut and clicks never skip the memories until one has been seen). MaskBeat holds the whisper and the name for at least its reading time (3 s, or 0.06 s per character), stretching memory_s and reveal_s if a line needs it. A click moves on a beat; after the first one, holding skips.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| full | {"build_s": 2.0, "rise_s": 2.4, "black_s": 0.6, "memory_s": [1.6, 1.8, 2.0], "reveal_s": 3.4, "push_in": 0.7} |
| short | {"build_s": 0.9, "rise_s": 1.4, "black_s": 0.7, "memory_s": [1.4, 2.0], "reveal_s": 3.4, "push_in": 0.6} |
| times_doc | build_s: the world quiets, the camera eases in, swell and heartbeat. rise_s: the Relic lifts to the face in slow motion while a ghostly porcelain face flickers over yours. black_s: the hard silence after contact. memory_s: one entry per memory frame of the fallen Hunter (their painted memories, or their face and then their splash: the same total shared out when the count differs), the last held with the whisper. reveal_s: the snap back to the end (pose, name and title, sting). push_in: how far the camera eases in (0..1 of the way to the face). |
| music_duck_db | -30 |
| heart_gaps_s | [0.62, 0.5, 0.4, 0.32] |
| whispers | {"gunslinger": "Another job. Another mark on the tally.", "juggernaut": "The blade is hungry. Feed it, or it feeds on you.", "archer": "Every mask I sewed, I will cut loose.", "bulwark": "Hold on. The shore is close.", "mage": "One day I give the storm back.", "ashwick": "Bottled Blight. Drink up.", "dredge": "Come down where it's quiet.", "tender": "Stay close to the light.", "rimewright": "Skate. Don't look down at the ice.", "dolm": "Stone remembers what eyes forget.", "ostra": "Go on, laugh. I'll keep it.", "thief": "I only meant to take a look.", "gil": "Ooh, what does this one do?"} |
| sting_semitones | {"gunslinger": 0, "juggernaut": -5, "archer": 3, "bulwark": -7, "mage": 5, "ashwick": 2, "dredge": -9, "tender": 7, "rimewright": 4, "dolm": -3, "ostra": 1, "thief": 6, "gil": 8} |
| sting_doc | Each Hunter's sting is the same rising motif in their own key (semitones from A3). |

## merge_forms (`content/rules/merge_forms.json`)

How a merge looks and plays (docs/decisions/0003). Forms with a kit live in content/merge_forms/<merge id>.json. This file holds the shared timings, the stat-style fallback every other Boki gets until its form is written (the Boki's type picks its look, rider and dash trail; the same for everyone, no tiers), and the weak surge.

## pet_react (`content/rules/pet_react.json`)

How a Boki answers a pat by personality (scripts/home/pet_react.gd, used by home.gd and interior.gd). Four kinds, picked from its traits: shy (low bravery), proud (high temper), playful (curious), sleepy (the rest). Each plays a short beat from the existing clips plus one mood icon, pays joy and trust, and pays at most `cap` times a farm day (the window is care.json care_day_s); past the cap it only looks at you.

|---|---|
| shy_bravery | 0.4 |
| proud_temper | 0.62 |
| playful_curiosity | 0.5 |
| again_s | 15 |

| love_joy | 7 |
| love_joy_doc | extra joy when the Boki's favourite play is being petted (before this a pat gave 12 to those and 5 to the rest). |
| hold_s | 1 |
| away_m | 4 |
| away_m_doc | m a proud Boki walks off after its one pat. |

## pickup (`content/rules/pickup.json`)

Ground pickup reach (scripts/match/pickup_reach.gd, docs/PICKUP_REACH.md). Each rule is a flat radius and a height (m) a hunter must be within, and nothing may stand between them and the thing: a rock, higher ground or a kit wall blocks a pickup as it blocks sight. walk: consumables, armor shards, gems, seeds, Rift and chest keys fly to you as you pass (no key); pull_speed + (radius - distance) x pull_gain m/s, taken when within grab m of your chest, settle s after they land. tune: a weapon tuning taken by walking over it. bot: a bot walking over a tuning or a gear piece better than its own. interact: gear and treasure, taken with the interact key; of several in reach the key takes the one nearest the cursor.

## shops (`content/rules/shops.json`)



| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| _doc | In-match shops (scripts/match/shops.gd, shop_stock.gd; the stock plan is docs/SOURCE_UTILITIES.md section 3). Vendors stand at the spots a hand-made map lists under islands[].shops ([x, z, theme]). Every vendor sells its theme's whole `sells` list, the same in every match: tonic and armor_kit everywhere, everything else in exactly one shop. The gems are the ones a hunter picked up this run, so spending means less to extract. Entries: a utility item id (content/utility), repair (armor back to full), armor_up (the next armor tier), backpack (the next pack tier, priced by Equal backpack_shop), boots:<gear id> (worn at boots_rar), perk:<perk id> (Data.PERKS). left = how many of one entry a vendor has (the host keeps count online). Never sold: keys, shards, the Revive Ember and anything found only in matches; the never list is what --shops-check scans for. Prices are run gems: utility items use their content price times util_k. |

## show_ring (`content/rules/show_ring.json`)

Show Ring, a judged show on a small stage near the Training post (briefs/design/GARDEN_MODERN.md 4.2 game 3, scripts/home/show_ring.gd). Only with farm_build.json base_mode on. Two rested Boki show: the one you back and a rival. Three rounds of up to 10 points each: Look (how it has been raised), Trick (three timed presses, the trick picked by its best stat) and Bond (it walks to you past a snack, a toy and the rival; you call as it passes each). Three judges post a taste for the week; each judge whose taste the Boki fits adds taste_bonus. Every score is worked out from the records and the presses only, so the same Boki and presses always score the same. Units: seconds, points, needs and trust 0-100, traits 0-1.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| look | {"joy": 2.0, "clean": 2.0, "lean": 2.0, "parts": 2.0, "aura": 1.0, "keepsakes": 1.0} |
| look_doc | Most points each part of Look gives (10 in all). joy and clean: in proportion to the need. lean: full points at a full lean ('in full colour'), half at half a lean or more. parts: one point a grown part level (rec.muts). aura: worn (rec.aura set). keepsakes: one point a Cup Ribbon kind held (rec.ribbons). |
| half_lean | 0.5 |
| half_lean_doc | Lean strength (Evo.lean, 0..1) that earns half the lean points. |
| tricks | {"power": {"name": "Log Lift", "line": "hoists a log three times"}, "guard": {"name": "Statue Stand", "line": "freezes in three proud poses"}, "speed": {"name": "Whirl Hop", "line": "spins through three quick hops"}, "focus": {"name": "Pebble Balance", "line": "balances three pebbles on its nose"}} |
| tricks_doc | The trick a Boki shows, by its highest trained stat (Care.STATS order on a tie). |
| press | {"great": 3.0, "good": 2.0, "miss": 0.0} |
| press_doc | Trick points a timed press grades to; three presses, so 9 at most. |
| stat_per_point | 0.02 |
| stat_doc | Trick points a point of the trick's stat adds, up to 1 (50 points of it). |
| trick_s | 25 |
| trick_doc | Seconds for the three presses; presses not made by then are misses. |
| lures | [{"id": "snack", "name": "a snack", "at": 0.25, "pull": 0.8}, {"id": "toy", "name": "a toy", "at": 0.5, "pull": 0.7}, {"id": "rival", "name": "its rival", "at": 0.75, "pull": 0.6}] |
| lures_doc | What it walks past, in order. at: share of the walk where it is level with the lure. pull: how far it strays (0..1) with no trust, no loyalty and no call. |
| trust_shrink | 0.5 |
| loyal_shrink | 0.4 |
| shrink_doc | Trust 100 takes trust_shrink off every pull, loyalty 1 takes loyal_shrink (shares of the pull, added). |
| call | {"great": 0.0, "good": 0.4, "miss": 1.0} |
| call_doc | Share of the pull left after your call for each lure. |
| call_great | 0.3 |
| call_good | 0.7 |
| call_window_doc | Seconds from the moment it is level with a lure: a call this close is great, then good; later or never is a miss. |
| walk_s | 42 |
| walk_m | 8 |
| walk_doc | The Bond walk: seconds and metres from the stage to you. |
| look_s | 30 |
| judge_s | 24 |
| rounds_doc | Seconds the Look parade and the judging take; with the trick and the walk the show runs about 2 minutes. |
| rival_press | {"great": 40, "good": 15} |
| rival_doc | The rival's handler: each of its trick presses is great at this many points of its trick stat, good at this many, else a miss; its calls are good. |
| judges | ["Old Bramwell", "Auntie Fennick", "Ludo Pebble"] |
| judges_doc | Judges' names when you have no retired mentors to sit on the bench (mentors go first). |

## snack_patch (`content/rules/snack_patch.json`)

The garden's one snack patch (scripts/home/snack_patch.gd, base_mode only; GARDEN.md section 10 question 1). It grows one of each snack in snacks every grow_secs and you pick them up by walking over it. They go to the pantry (Save.d crops) to feed the element-lean foods; the patch is never sold and has no seed, shop or water chore.

|---|---|
| snacks | ["emberberry", "tidebloom", "sunroot", "puffcorn"] |

Every food in lean.json is in exactly one list (--lean-snacks-check). A patch on a theme with a list grows that list; the key is the home_layout THEMES id. |

## status_looks (`content/rules/status_looks.json`)

The plain statuses on a Hunter's body (scripts/combat/status_looks.gd, docs/STATUS_LOOKS.md). Each status names its look (a builder in the script), its colours (the owning Hunter's ability colours where one Hunter owns the status), `y` (m, where the look sits on a 2 m body; scaled with the Hunter), `size` (scale) and `pace` (animation speed). Every look has its own shape, place and motion, so two statuses never read alike even in grey; none lies flat on the ground (a ground ring means gameplay). Every source (a kit, a Boki, a monster) shows the one look, sized to the body's hitbox.

## toys (`content/rules/toys.json`)

The Boki base's playthings (GARDEN.md section 4; only while farm_build.json base_mode is on). A Boki at home with a joy below joy_below picks a toy on its own, walks to it, plays play_secs and gains one point of the toy's stat (Care.add_stat, capped by level as today) and joy. Each toy has the clip a rigged Boki plays at it (BokiHomeClips, set as the kact meta). Units: seconds, tiles, 0..1 trait values, joy points.
